(25 July 2010){{cite web|title=KCB - AFC Leopards (25/07-2010 kl. 16:00)|url=http://www.futaa.com//football/event/793658|publisher=Futaa.com|date=25 July 2010|accessdate=17 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524165606/http://www.futaa.com/football/event/793658|archive-date=24 May 2013|url-status=dead}} |matches=240 |total goals=455 |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |prevseason=[[2009 Kenyan Premier League|2009]] |nextseason=[[2011 Kenyan Premier League|2011]] }} The '''2010 Kenyan Premier League''' was the seventh season of the [[Kenyan Premier League]] since it started in 2003 and the forty-seventh season of top division [[Association football|football]] in [[Kenya]] since 1963. It began on 20 February with [[Mahakama F.C.|Mahakama]] and [[Sony Sugar F.C.|Sony Sugar]] and ended on 14 November with [[Nairobi City Stars]] and [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]]. [[Sofapaka F.C.|Sofapaka]] had previously won the title but [[Ulinzi Stars F.C.|Ulinzi Stars]] finished top. [[Sofapaka F.C.|Sofapaka]] still won the [[2010 Kenyan Super Cup]] after defeating 12-time champions [[A.F.C. Leopards]]. After staying in the league for an entire [[decade]], [[Red Berets F.C.|Red Berets]], who were only two points behind [[Kenya Commercial Bank S.C.|KCB]] when they were relegated along with previously promoted [[Mahakama F.C.|Mahakama]], disbanded to immense pressure from its sponsors to produce good performances.{{cite news |title=Red Berets FC disbanded |url=http://www.michezoafrika.com/Kpl/Red-Berets-FC-disbanded/896.aspx |author=Dennis Machio |publisher=MichezoAfrika.com |date=27 January 2011 |accessdate=17 May 2012}} The two teams had replaced [[Bandari F.C. (Kenya)|Bandari]] and [[Agrochemical F.C.|Agrochemical]], the former gaining promotion once again for the [[2011 Kenyan Premier League|next season]]. ==Changes from last season== '''Relegated from [[Kenyan Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[Agrochemical F.C.|Agrochemical]] * [[Bandari F.C.
